The pulse

As a bell contracts, the change in its pulse pushes the pair around the orbit and upward. Water drag slows both motions between pushes.

The trailing strands

Each strand is a chain with fixed link lengths. The wake pulls the strands inward as the swimmers come together.

The heart

The scene blends the swimming mesh toward a heart profile. The camera comes around to a broadside view, where the two bells read as the lobes.

Scientific references

Bell pulses and the wake

In the released model, bell contractions propel the pair around the orbit and upward. A simplified wake pulls the trailing strands inward. The pulse and wake coefficients were tuned for the duet.

  • The early storyboard used the study’s observations of energy recapture to explore a second, gentler push as the bell relaxes.

    Gemmell et al. (2013) · Passive energy recapture in jellyfish contributes to propulsive advantage over other metazoans

  • The study of interacting vortex rings beneath a moon jellyfish’s bell informed the early storyboard’s pulsed wake. The released duet represents the wake’s pull with a simplified flow.

    Gemmell et al. (2021) · The most efficient metazoan swimmer creates a ‘virtual wall’ to enhance performance
